title: The whole of it
hook: Ananda says good friendship is half the holy life; no, the whole (SN 45.2)

segments.voice: Yesterday: grass, clay and the line of mothers, and your line, anyone may have been family. Who did you treat as family? Today Ananda makes a guess about friendship, and closes our week by being corrected. Day six hundred fifty-one.

A friend drags someone to the gym on a cold morning. Another says, kindly, that a relationship isn't doing them any good. A third just keeps showing up, again and again, until the other person starts showing up too. Ananda, the Buddha's attendant, has been thinking about friendship. He comes to the Buddha in a Sakyan town and says, with some confidence, that he's worked out how much good friends are worth. He's about to be told he's off by half. Today: kalyanamitta.
screen: `THE FRIEND WHO GETS YOU THERE.` → `ANANDA HAS A THEORY.` → `OFF BY HALF.`

segments.voice: SN 45.2 is short and has a surprise in the middle. Ananda says: half of the holy life, venerable sir, is good friendship, good companionship, good comradeship. A generous estimate. The Buddha's reply is immediate. Not so, Ananda, not so. Good friendship, good companionship, good comradeship is the entire holy life. Then he explains. When someone has a good friend, you can expect them to develop the noble eightfold path. Right view, right intention, all the way through. A good friend doesn't just help with the path. They're how the path gets walked. Then he points to himself. It's by relying on me as a good friend, the Buddha says, that beings subject to birth are freed from birth, beings subject to aging, from aging, subject to sorrow, from sorrow. The teacher calls himself a friend. The Pali phrase is kalyanamittata, having a lovely friend, a good friend. Kalyana means beautiful, good, and mitta means friend. It doesn't mean someone who agrees with everything. Another discourse in the Numbered Sayings sketches a good friend as one who speaks up, can bear to be spoken to, and doesn't lead you toward what harms. Look back at this week. One arrow instead of two. Foam on the river. The burden, and putting it down. A dog circling its post. Tears more than the oceans. A line of mothers with no beginning. Heavy material, most of it. And the week ends here, with the Buddha saying that the way through all of it is walked with friends.
screen: `HALF THE HOLY LIFE, SAYS ANANDA` · `NOT SO: THE ENTIRE HOLY LIFE` · `THE BUDDHA AS A GOOD FRIEND` · `KALYANAMITTA: A LOVELY FRIEND` · then, large: `THE WHOLE OF IT.`

segments.voice: Sit, and bring to mind one good friend. Someone who has helped you become a little more yourself, a little kinder, a little braver. See their face. Remember one specific time they showed up for you. Let gratitude fill the chest without pushing it. Then, if you'd like, hold a simple wish for them: may you be well. After the bell, if it's possible, call them, or send a short message. The bell holds the time.
kalyanamitta. The Pali term for a good or lovely friend, used in SN 45.2 when the Buddha tells Ananda that good friendship is not half but the entire holy life. Today's word.
Your line: walked with friends. Call or message one good friend today, and tell them, in your own words, one thing they've helped you with. Day six hundred fifty-one.

screen: `DAY 651 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: ALL IS BURNING, READ WHOLE.`

howItsDone: Buddhist communities across traditions practice together in sanghas, temples and retreat groups, and teachers often cite this sutta when they speak about spiritual friendship.

myth: the Buddha agrees good friendship is half the holy life
he says not so: it is the entire holy life.
in SN 45.2 the Buddha calls himself a good friend
by relying on him as a good friend, beings are freed from birth, aging and sorrow.
in the texts a good friend is one who agrees with everything
a good friend speaks up, can bear to be spoken to, and doesn't lead you toward harm.

fork.setup: you're Ananda. you've thought it through and tell the Buddha good friendship is half the holy life. what does he say?
options: not so: it is the entire holy life.
friendship has nothing to do with it.
fork.reveal: he corrects Ananda at once: good friendship is the whole of the holy life, because with a good friend the path gets walked.

original.note: Pali kalyanamitta: a good or lovely friend; kalyanamittata is good friendship.

trapdoor: what you thought: the whole of it is about being a loyal friend.
what it means: in SN 45.2, good friendship is not half but the entire holy life, because with a good friend one develops the eightfold path.
what a scholar hears: SN 45 is the Magga Samyutta, the chapter on the path; the same exchange appears again in SN 3.18, where the Buddha tells it to King Pasenadi.
recall: as he says, so he does

sources.ref: Anguttara Nikaya 7.37 (Dutiyamitta Sutta), qualities of a good friend

notes: SN 45.2 paraphrased. Confirm the setting (Sakkara, a town of the Sakyans), Ananda's statement (half the holy life is good friendship, companionship, comradeship), the Buddha's correction (the entire holy life), the explanation (one with a good friend develops the noble eightfold path) and 'by relying on me as a good friend...'.

The qualities of a good friend are general (e.g. AN 7.36: gives what is hard to give, bears with you, tells secrets, keeps yours, does not abandon in misfortune); described loosely as 'speaks honestly, can bear to be told things'.
Confirm that SN 3.18 retells the exchange to Pasenadi (trapdoor).
Year one (days 100, 198) touched friendship; this day reads the Ananda exchange itself.

Review (y2 editor pass): the hook opened 'Think of...' and told the listener about their own friends; rewritten as third-person scenes. Cut the unsupported 'small' town. The good-friend qualities are now tied to AN 7.37 (added to sources; confirm numbering and that 'a speaker, patient with being spoken to, does not urge toward what is baseless' is fairly paraphrased). HOW no longer says 'every tradition'.
